slides.say: At a conference, one quarter of the participants attend the morning workshop, one sixth attend the evening workshop, and one twelfth attend both. Exactly four participants attend both. How many participants attend neither workshop?

So they ask for neither. We get fractions, and one real number of people, four. Every fact is here, so it's an exact question. We'll solve it in two different ways. The squares method in fractions, and then by finding the number of participants first.
Let's start with the math way, the squares method, with fractions. Like in the lesson, the givens are fractions of the participants, so all the participants together are one whole.
We draw four boxes. Neither, evening only, both, and morning only. All four together are one. The morning bracket is a quarter, and the evening bracket is a sixth.
Both is a twelfth, so we write a twelfth in the middle box.
Evening only is a sixth minus a twelfth. A sixth is two twelfths. Two twelfths minus one twelfth is one twelfth.
Now let's find neither. Not in the morning is one minus a quarter, three quarters. That's neither plus evening only, the boxes outside the morning bracket.
at: Not in the morning is one minus

slides.say: Three quarters is nine twelfths. Take away evening only, one twelfth, and we get eight twelfths. So neither is eight twelfths.
But the choices are numbers of people. The question says the twelfth in both is four people. So each twelfth is four people, and we have eight twelfths. Eight times four is thirty-two people.
Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now an insight, so we don't work with fractions at all. We start again from the givens. A twelfth of the participants is four people. So all the participants are twelve times four, forty-eight.
Now let's write everything in people. The morning is a quarter of forty-eight, twelve. The evening is a sixth of forty-eight, eight. And four are in both.
Evening only is eight minus four, four.
Not in the morning is forty-eight minus twelve, thirty-six. That's neither plus evening only.
So neither is thirty-six minus four, thirty-two. The same thirty-two.
Careful with choice number four, twenty-eight. That's forty-eight minus twelve minus eight. It takes the four in both away twice.
And choice number one, sixteen, is everyone in at least one workshop. Twelve plus eight minus four is sixteen. But they asked for neither.
So when fractions come with one real number of people, find the total first, and work in people. Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
